# FDA Guidance: Q-Submission Program

**Full Title**: Requests for Feedback and Meetings for Medical Device Submissions: The Q-Submission Program
**Document Date**: May 28, 2025
**Status**: Final
**PDF Source**: https://www.fda.gov/media/128149/download
**Issuing Body**: CDRH, CBER
**Docket Number**: FDA-2018-D-1774

## Scope

The Q-Submission Program provides a mechanism for device manufacturers to obtain FDA feedback on planned marketing submissions, IDE submissions, and CLIA waiver applications before formal filing. It covers multiple types of interactions between sponsors and FDA review teams.

This guidance does not cover PMA Day 100 Meetings, Breakthrough Device Designation Requests, or Accessory Classification Requests (each has separate guidance).

## Key Requirements

### Types of Q-Submissions

| Q-Sub Type | Purpose | Feedback Format |
|------------|---------|-----------------|
| **Pre-Submission (Pre-Sub) -- Meeting Request** | Feedback on a planned marketing submission, IDE, or CLIA Waiver; includes a scheduled meeting | Written feedback + teleconference or face-to-face meeting |
| **Pre-Submission (Pre-Sub) -- Written Feedback Only** | Same purpose but without a meeting | Written feedback only |
| **Submission Issue Request (SIR)** | Discuss outstanding review issues from a hold or clinical hold letter | Written feedback OR meeting (submitter specifies) |
| **Informational Meeting Request** | Present information to FDA without expectation of official feedback | Interactive dialogue; no formal written feedback |
| **Study Risk Determination** | Obtain SR or NSR determination for a planned clinical study | Written determination |

### Pre-Submission Submission Content — III.B(1) "Submission Content" and III.B(4)(a)(1) "Additional Recommended Submission Contents"

_Heading relabeled 2026-09-08 (task ben/123) to the source-md section names; "Pre-Submission Package Contents" is not a heading in the guidance._

**Required Elements:**
- Cover letter -- stating this is a Pre-Submission; specifying meeting or written feedback only
- Device description -- clear description of the device, components, and function
- Intended use / Indications for use -- proposed intended use statement
- Proposed predicate device(s) -- if applicable, with comparison
- Specific questions for FDA -- focused, well-defined (recommend 3-4 substantial topics maximum)
- Supporting information -- sufficient context for FDA to understand and respond
- Proposed regulatory pathway -- intended submission type (510(k), De Novo, PMA, IDE, etc.)
- Administrative information -- contact information, device name, product code (if known)

**Recommended but Situational:**
- Proposed testing/study protocols
- Proposed clinical study design
- Preliminary performance data
- Risk analysis summary
- Comparison table (device vs. predicate)
- Literature references

**Format:**
- Electronic copy (eCopy) submitted to FDA Document Control Center
- Table of contents for organized navigation

### FDA Response Timelines (MDUFA Commitments)

| Milestone | Timeline |
|-----------|----------|
| Acceptance Review (RTA) | Within 15 business days of receipt |
| Meeting date determined | By Day 30 |
| Written feedback provided (meeting request) | By Day 70 or 5 business days before meeting, whichever is sooner |
| Written feedback (no meeting) | By Day 70 |
| Meeting held | Typically Day 75-90 |
| Submitter drafts meeting minutes | Within 15 calendar days of meeting |
| FDA reviews meeting minutes | Within 30 days of receipt |

**SIR Timelines (Two-Tier System):**
- SIR received within 60 days of FDA's letter: feedback within 21 days
- SIR received more than 60 days after: feedback within 70 days

**Key Notes:**
- Pre-Submissions are the only Q-Sub type with MDUFA commitments
- No user fees are associated with Q-Submissions
- Completeness of the submission package is not required -- include only information sufficient for the review team to respond to questions

### Meeting Procedures

**Meeting Formats:**
- Teleconference (most common, easier to schedule)
- Face-to-face (when demos needed)
- Written feedback only (when questions are straightforward)

**Meeting Details:**
- Typically 60 minutes
- Written feedback provided before the meeting (review beforehand to focus discussion)
- Submitter is responsible for drafting meeting minutes
- Requesting a meeting upfront is recommended -- easier to cancel than to add later

### Multiple Pre-Subs for the Same Device

- Allowed, but avoid having multiple open simultaneously for the same device/indication
- Sequential Pre-Subs on different topics are tracked as supplements in the same Q-Sub family
- If topics are close together in timing, combine into one Pre-Sub (up to 3-4 topics)
- Different indications for the same device may justify separate concurrent Pre-Subs

### FDA Feedback Stability

FDA intends that Pre-Sub feedback will not change, provided:
1. Information in the future marketing submission is consistent with the Pre-Sub
2. Data or other information does not raise important new issues materially affecting safety or effectiveness

### PCCP Strategy Discussion

Pre-Submissions explicitly support discussion of PCCP strategy as part of regulatory strategy for planned marketing submissions. The PCCP guidance specifically encourages sponsors to use Pre-Submissions to discuss PCCP plans before filing.

Recommended PCCP-related Pre-Sub topics:
- Proposed PCCP scope and appropriateness for the device type
- Proposed change categories and their definitions
- Proposed modification protocols and validation methodologies
- Performance criteria and acceptance thresholds

### Predicate Discussion

Predicate device selection and substantial equivalence arguments are core Pre-Sub topics. Sponsors can discuss proposed predicates, SE arguments, technology comparisons, intended use alignment, and performance testing strategy.

## Key Definitions

| Term | Definition |
|------|-----------|
| **Q-Submission** | Any formal request for feedback from FDA on a medical device, tracked through the Q-Submission system |
| **Pre-Submission (Pre-Sub)** | A Q-Sub type for obtaining feedback on planned marketing submissions, IDEs, or CLIA waivers |
| **Submission Issue Request (SIR)** | A Q-Sub type for discussing outstanding issues from FDA review letters |
| **RTA (Refuse to Accept)** | FDA's initial determination of whether a Pre-Sub meets minimum content requirements |
| **Q-Sub Family** | Related Q-Subs for the same device/indication, tracked together with supplements and amendments |

## Submission Requirements

### Practical Timeline for Planning

```
Day 0:    Pre-Sub submitted
Day 15:   RTA acceptance (or refuse -- requires resubmission)
Day 30:   Meeting date scheduled (if meeting requested)
Day 65-70: Written feedback received
Day 70-90: Meeting held (if requested)
Day 90-105: Meeting minutes submitted
Day 105-135: FDA reviews minutes
Day 135+:  Incorporate feedback into submission drafting
```

Minimum recommended lead time before planned marketing submission: **4-5 months** to allow for full Pre-Sub cycle plus incorporation time.

### After Submission

- Monitor for RTA decision within 15 business days
- If RTA refused: address deficiencies and resubmit promptly
- Prepare for meeting by reviewing written feedback
- Draft and submit meeting minutes within 15 calendar days
- Incorporate FDA feedback into submission documents

### Ongoing Q-Sub Management

- Track Q-Sub family for follow-up submissions
- Ensure marketing submission consistency with Pre-Sub representations (preserves feedback stability)
